baselineSpikesPerSec.note: Round resting rate in the mammalian canal-afferent range. Not copied from a checked table. Goldberg JM, Fernandez C. J Neurophysiol. 1971;34(4):635-660 is the usual squirrel-monkey paper; the 90 was not read off that page.

afferentGainSpikesPerDegPerSec.note: Set so baseline/gain equals inhibitorySaturationDegPerSec (60 deg/s). Excitation stays linear; inhibition reaches 0 spikes/s at that canal velocity. Not copied from a checked table.

cupulaTimeConstantSec.source: Raphan T. Vestibular, locomotor, and vestibulo-autonomic research: 50 years of collaboration with Bernard Cohen. J Neurophysiol. 123(1):329-345. doi:10.1152/jn.00485.2019. That review says the human cupular time constant is about 4 s (Dai et al. 1999) and the monkey afferent time constant is about 3.5–5 s (Goldberg and Fernandez 1971). The 4 s figure is taken from that sentence.
cupulaTimeConstantSec.note: Dominant cupula (long) time constant. The short mechanical time constant is not modelled.

velocityStorageSec.source: Raphan T, Matsuo V, Cohen B. Velocity storage in the vestibulo-ocular reflex arc (VOR). Exp Brain Res. 1979;35:229-248. Cited for the mechanism. The 16 s value was not copied from a table in that paper.
velocityStorageSec.note: Round teaching value for a central time constant longer than the cupula. Unverified.

vorGain.note: Raises the canal-plane plant so a pure yaw, whose horizontal-canal cosine is about 0.95, still produces a horizontal eye velocity near the head velocity. Not a measured human constant.

plantScale.note: Agonist contraction and antagonist relaxation each carry the canal axis, so 0.5 keeps the pair from adding twice. Model coefficient, not a measured constant.

fastPhaseThresholdDeg.note: Eye-position magnitude that starts a reset toward the centre. The fast phase is this reset, so nystagmus is not scripted as a separate animation.

fastPhaseSpeedDegPerSec.note: Reset speed while the eye is past the threshold. Not copied from a checked table.

fastPhaseStopDeg.note: The reset ends inside this distance of the centre, or as soon as it would cross the centre.

inhibitorySaturationDegPerSec.source: Ewald JR. Physiologische Untersuchungen über das Endorgan des Nervus octavus. Wiesbaden: Bergmann; 1892. Second law: excitation is a stronger canal stimulus than inhibition, because firing can rise well above rest and can only fall to zero. Halmagyi GM, Curthoys IS. A clinical sign of canal paresis. Arch Neurol. 1988;45(7):737-739. A rapid head impulse shows that asymmetry after one labyrinth is lost. The 60 deg/s clip is a model setting so a lesion-side impulse near 200 deg/s keeps only a small gain; it was not copied from a table.
inhibitorySaturationDegPerSec.note: Canal velocity at which the inhibitory afferent stops decreasing. Excitation is not clipped in this range.

staticImbalanceGain.note: Tuning value, unverified. Not copied from a table. It scales a constant resting-rate loss before the eyes move. Without it, a dead canal looks like a continuous impulse at the full inhibitory cutoff and the spontaneous nystagmus is far too fast. 0.9 was chosen so a complete right loss sits near 20 deg/s of horizontal slow phase.

verticalRestingScale.note: Tuning value, unverified. Not copied from a table. Vertical-canal resting loss is multiplied by staticImbalanceGain and then by this 0.45, so the resting roll does not overwhelm the horizontal beat. Dynamic head-movement responses are not multiplied by this number.

torsionalVorGain.source: Tweed D, Sievering D, Misslisch H, Fetter M, Zee DS, Koenig E. Rotational kinematics of the human vestibuloocular reflex. I. Gain matrices. J Neurophysiol. 1994;72(5):2467-2479. The abstract gives a torsional collinear gain of about 0.37 for 0.3 Hz rotation in darkness. This file uses 0.35, inside that low range.
torsionalVorGain.note: Multiplies the roll component of slow-phase eye velocity. Horizontal and vertical components are left on vorGain.

torsionalStorageSec.note: Vertical-canal velocity storage. Shorter than the horizontal 16 s so post-rotatory roll does not linger. The number was not copied from a checked table.

catchUpThresholdDeg.note: Tuning value, unverified. Gaze slip that starts one catch-up saccade when head speed is high and the slow-phase gain is low. Timing is simplified: one saccade per impulse, at the fast-phase speed, ending when the slip falls or the eye passes about 35 degrees. This is not a full saccade generator.

catchUpMinHeadDegPerSec.note: Head speed above which a weak slow phase may trigger a catch-up saccade. Ordinary nystagmus at lower speed still uses the position reset.
